subject: Chemistry
basis: LABEL SEMANTICS: 'CBSE Class 12' here means the CBSE/NCERT CHEMISTRY CURRICULUM across
Std XI + XII, not the Class-12 board paper alone. It has to: several State Board Std XII
chapters (Ionic Equilibria, Chemical Thermodynamics) are NCERT CLASS 11 chapters, and
the school's own mapper uses 'Not for CBSE' to decide what to teach in Std XI.
PRIMARY SOURCE: the NCERT books on disk, which are the current RATIONALISED editions -
Class 11 has 9 chapters (Some Basic Concepts, Structure of Atom, Classification and
Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Thermodynamics, Equilibrium, Redox, Organic Basics,
Hydrocarbons) and Class 12 has 10 (Solutions, Electrochemistry, Chemical Kinetics,
d- and f-Block, Coordination Compounds, Haloalkanes and Haloarenes, Alcohols/Phenols/
Ethers, Aldehydes/Ketones/Carboxylic Acids, Amines, Biomolecules). Pre-rationalisation
editions had 14 and 16 - the deletions are what most 'not' rulings below rest on.
Both books were verified by EXTRACTING their contents, not by reading filenames:
Class 11 = 9 chapters / 238 numbered sections, Class 12 = 10 chapters / 97 sections.
BANK VALIDATION IS ONLY PARTIAL, AND THAT IS STATED HONESTLY: the question bank holds
NO CBSE Chemistry questions (CBSE Class 12 is Mathematics-only, 521 q). NEET was used as
a proxy because NEET is NCERT-based, and it corroborates six deletions - Solid State,
States of Matter, Surface Chemistry, Polymers, Chemistry in Everyday Life and
Environmental Chemistry all have ZERO NEET PYQs since 2024 (last seen 2023).
THE PROXY'S LIMIT, found rather than assumed: NEET still asks p-Block heavily (27 PYQs,
16 of them since 2024) even though the rationalised NCERT books carry no p-block chapter.
NEET follows the NMC syllabus, which retained p-block, so NEET presence does NOT imply
CBSE inclusion. The p-block rulings below therefore follow the NCERT books, not NEET.

chapters.note: NCERT Class 11 Ch.1 Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry.

No standalone NCERT analytical-chemistry chapter, but this chapter's substance is NCERT Class 11 Ch.1: significant figures and uncertainty in measurement (1.4), percentage composition and empirical/molecular formula (1.9), stoichiometry, limiting reagent and reactions in solutions (1.10). Note this is the chapter the school's 2026-27 plan skips - for a CBSE-track student that removes core Class 11 content.
NCERT Class 11 Ch.8 section 8.8 Methods of Purification - sublimation, crystallisation, distillation, differential extraction, chromatography.
NCERT Class 11 Ch.2 Structure of Atom.
NCERT Class 11 Ch.4 Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure. NCERT also puts hydrogen bonding here (4.9), whereas the State Board teaches it inside States of Matter.
NCERT Class 11 Ch.7 Redox Reactions.
NCERT Class 11 Ch.3 Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties.
The rationalised NCERT has no s-Block chapter and no Hydrogen chapter; both were deleted. NEET still asks a little s-block (7 PYQs) but on the NMC syllabus, not the NCERT books.

The rationalised NCERT has no p-Block chapter in either Class 11 or Class 12. NEET asks p-block heavily (16 PYQs since 2024) but under the NMC syllabus, which retained it - that is a NEET-vs-CBSE divergence, not CBSE coverage.
States of Matter was deleted from NCERT Class 11. Corroborated: 0 NEET PYQs since 2024 (last 2023).
Surface Chemistry was deleted from NCERT Class 12. Corroborated: 0 NEET PYQs since 2024 (last 2023).
NCERT Class 11 Ch.6 Equilibrium, sections 6.1-6.8 (physical and chemical equilibrium, Kc/Kp, Le Chatelier).
No nuclear-chemistry or radioactivity chapter in NCERT Class 11 or 12.
NCERT Class 11 Ch.8 Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques.
NCERT Class 11 Ch.9 Hydrocarbons.
Chemistry in Everyday Life was deleted from NCERT Class 12. Corroborated: 0 NEET PYQs since 2024 (last 2023).
Solid State was deleted from NCERT Class 12. Corroborated: 0 NEET PYQs since 2024 (last 2023). Still fully in CET.
NCERT Class 12 Ch.1 Solutions.

In syllabus, but as NCERT CLASS 11 Ch.6 (Equilibrium, sections 6.9-6.13: acids/bases, pH, buffers, Ksp). The State Board defers this to Std XII, so a CBSE-track student meets it a year earlier - a sequencing difference, not a gap.
In syllabus, but as NCERT CLASS 11 Ch.5 Thermodynamics - again a year earlier than the State Board sequence. This is the chapter the school's plan sources from NCERT for exactly that reason.
NCERT Class 12 Ch.2 Electrochemistry.
NCERT Class 12 Ch.3 Chemical Kinetics.
No p-Block chapter in the rationalised NCERT. Same NEET divergence as Std XI Ch.9. Still fully in CET.
NCERT Class 12 Ch.4 The d- and f-Block Elements.
NCERT Class 12 Ch.5 Coordination Compounds.
NCERT Class 12 Ch.6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes.
NCERT Class 12 Ch.7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers.
NCERT Class 12 Ch.8 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids.
NCERT Class 12 Ch.9 Amines.
NCERT Class 12 Ch.10 Biomolecules.
Polymers was deleted from NCERT Class 12. Corroborated: 0 NEET PYQs since 2024 (last 2023). Still fully in CET.
No green-chemistry or nanochemistry chapter; Environmental Chemistry, its nearest NCERT relative, was deleted. Corroborated: 0 NEET PYQs since 2024. Still fully in CET.
